grh_57431b74a4bd5ab3d99b.title: The Dishonest Boy
paragraphs: Russell Brandt steals his poor report card before his parents can see it and tries to shift suspicion onto Ira Nelson, his father's elderly longtime bookkeeper. The lie becomes dangerous because Mr. Brandt has already been considering dismissing Ira as no longer useful to the business. Dr. Christian questions Russell closely, catches the contradictions in his story and forces him to admit that he took the report card and falsely accused Ira. When Russell finally confesses, Dr. Christian reminds his angry father that honesty and courage are learned rather than automatic, and that Russell's lie did not create the father's willingness to discard a loyal old employee. The boy is held accountable, but his decision to tell the truth becomes the beginning of making things right.

grh_57462cdd6925af0d3e9d.title: Live Forever
paragraphs: A man terrified of death is carried in a vision into a future where science has made human beings effectively immortal. Instead of paradise, he finds an overcrowded society dominated forever by the same ancient people, while younger generations have no work, authority or purpose.
